metadata.name: Catch 2
metadata.notes:
Catch, drawn in single pixels, on Reference CPU 2 (its program is scripts/catch2.asm).

Set the speed to 10,000, press Run, click the keyboard and hold Left or Right. A block two pixels square falls in any column; the paddle, eight pixels wide, moves one pixel at a time. Catch a block to score on the two hex digits and make the next fall faster. A miss halts the CPU, and Reset plays again.

Every pixel is drawn by one routine, toggle, which the game calls seven times from four routines. It finds the pixel's screen byte and bit through another routine, locate, and flips the bit with XOR.

props.label: Program
props.source:
; Catch 2 (ADR 0036): Catch with single pixels, on Reference CPU 2.
; A block 2 pixels square falls in any of 63 columns; catch it with the paddle, 8 pixels wide,
; which Left and Right move one pixel at a time. A catch scores on HEX and the next block falls
; faster. A miss halts: Reset to play again.
;
; Every pixel is drawn or erased by one routine, toggle, which finds the screen byte and the bit
; through another, locate, and flips the bit. test finds a pixel through locate too.
;
; RAM: 0 paddle's left column, 1 block's column, 2 block's top row, 3 next block's column,
;      4 delay, 5 score, 6 wait count, 7 loop count, 8 column and 9 row for locate,
;      10 and 11 locate's scratch: row * 8, then the bit.

start:  LDI 28
        STA 0           ; the paddle starts at columns 28 to 35
        STA 3           ; and the first block falls above it
        LDI 60
        STA 4           ; DELAY: wait rounds per row
        LDI 31
        STA 9           ; the paddle's row
        LDI 0
        STA 7
paddle: LDA 0           ; draw it: 8 pixels
        ADD 7
        STA 8
        CALL toggle
        LDA 7
        ADI 1
        STA 7
        SBI 8
        JNZ paddle

spawn:  LDA 3           ; a new block at the top, in the next column
        STA 1
        ADI 23          ; next column: + 23, mod 63, so all 63 come in turn
        STA 3
        SBI 63
        JC wrap
        JMP top
wrap:   STA 3
top:    LDI 0
        STA 2
        STA 9
        CALL pair
        LDI 1
        STA 9
        CALL pair

row:    LDA 4           ; wait
        STA 6
wait:   LDA 6
        SBI 1
        STA 6
        JNZ wait
        CALL keys       ; the paddle moves up to two pixels a row
        CALL keys
        LDA 2           ; fall one row: erase the top, draw below the bottom
        STA 9
        CALL pair
        LDA 2
        ADI 2
        STA 9
        CALL pair
        LDA 2
        ADI 1
        STA 2
        SBI 29          ; on rows 29 and 30, just above the paddle: landed
        JNZ row

        LDI 31          ; is the paddle under both of the block's columns?
        STA 9
        LDA 1
        STA 8
        CALL test
        JZ miss
        LDA 1
        ADI 1
        STA 8
        CALL test
        JZ miss
        LDI 29          ; caught: erase the block
        STA 9
        CALL pair
        LDI 30
        STA 9
        CALL pair
        LDA 5           ; score
        ADI 1
        STA 5
        STA 0xFC        ; HEX
        LDA 4           ; faster, down to a delay of 6
        SBI 6
        STA 4
        JNZ spawn
        LDI 6
        STA 4
        JMP spawn
miss:   HLT

; keys: moves the paddle a pixel if Left or Right is held, unless it is at that edge.
keys:   LDA 0xFF        ; Left 0x82, Right 0x83
        SBI 0x82
        JZ left
        SBI 1
        JZ right
        RET
left:   LDA 0
        JZ edge         ; at the left edge
        LDI 31
        STA 9
        LDA 0
        ADI 7           ; erase its rightmost pixel
        STA 8
        CALL toggle
        LDA 0
        SBI 1
        STA 0
        STA 8           ; draw one more on the left
        CALL toggle
edge:   RET
right:  LDA 0
        SBI 56
        JZ edge         ; at the right edge
        LDI 31
        STA 9
        LDA 0
        STA 8           ; erase its leftmost pixel
        CALL toggle
        LDA 0
        ADI 1
        STA 0
        ADI 7           ; draw one more on the right
        STA 8
        CALL toggle
        RET

; pair: toggles the block's two pixels on row RAM[9].
pair:   LDA 1
        STA 8
        CALL toggle
        LDA 1
        ADI 1
        STA 8
        CALL toggle
        RET

; toggle: flips the pixel at column RAM[8], row RAM[9].
toggle: CALL locate
        LDA 11
        XOR 0xFD        ; SDATA
        STA 0xFD
        RET

; test: Z is 1 if the pixel at column RAM[8], row RAM[9] is dark.
test:   CALL locate
        LDA 11
        AND 0xFD
        RET

; locate: SPTR to the byte of the pixel at column RAM[8], row RAM[9], and RAM[11] to its bit.
; The bit is 0x80 shifted right by the column's low three bits, taken one at a time, with NOPs
; where a shift is not done, so it takes the same time whatever the column.
locate: LDA 9
        SHL
        SHL
        SHL
        STA 10          ; row * 8
        LDA 8
        SHR
        SHR
        SHR             ; column / 8
        ADD 10
        STA 0xFE        ; SPTR
        LDI 0x80
        STA 11
        LDA 8
        ANI 4
        JZ no4
        LDA 11
        SHR
        SHR
        SHR
        SHR
        STA 11
        JMP by2
no4:    NOP
        NOP
        NOP
        NOP
        NOP
        NOP
        NOP
by2:    LDA 8
        ANI 2
        JZ no2
        LDA 11
        SHR
        SHR
        STA 11
        JMP by1
no2:    NOP
        NOP
        NOP
        NOP
        NOP
by1:    LDA 8
        ANI 1
        JZ no1
        LDA 11
        SHR
        STA 11
        JMP done
no1:    NOP
        NOP
        NOP
        NOP
done:   RET

notes.text:
Devices
Data addresses 0xFC to 0xFF: KEY, the
key held; the screen's byte SPTR, SDATA;
HEX on two digits. OUT, shown here.

Clock and phase
Two cycles an instruction: T = 0 fetch,
T = 1 execute. HLT sets H.
Fetch = ¬T ∧ ¬H, Halted = H.

Fetch (PC, program ROM, IR)
IR ← ROM[PC], PC ← PC + 1. A jump
that is taken overrides it; RET puts
STACK in the PC. n is IR's operand.

Memory and I/O
n decoded: 0xF0-0xFF are I/O, so RAM
writes are gated off above 0xEF. The
read bus gives RAM[n]: RAM or a device.

Control
The whole high byte of IR addresses the
control ROM. Its bits are gated by the
phase: they act in the execute cycle.

Jumps
JMP, JZ if Z, JC if C, JNZ if not Z:
in the execute cycle, the PC takes n.

Registers (A, Z)
A takes n, RAM[n], ALU or logic.
Z ← 1 if the new A is 0.

ALU
A + B, or A − B as A + ¬B + 1. B is
RAM[n] or n. ALU is the sum; C takes
its carry, or the bit a shift dropped.

Logic unit
AND, OR and XOR of A with B, or A
shifted (SHL, SHR): its result is logic.

Shifts
A moved one bit left (SHL) or right
(SHR), and the bit it drops.

Stack
16 bytes and a 4-bit pointer, SP.
CALL writes PC at SP, then SP + 1;
RET reads at SP − 1 into STACK.
